title: How do we construct a kite with diagonals of 6 cm and 8 cm?
description: A kite is built from its two diagonals. The shorter diagonal is drawn first, then a line at right angles through its middle carries the longer diagonal, with its ends two and six centimetres from the crossing. Joining the four ends in order gives the kite, and the sides are checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: one diagonal of a kite cuts the other in half at right angles, so the longer diagonal sits on the line through the middle of the shorter one. Watch for students who put the crossing at the middle of both diagonals and draw a rhombus.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 2)
video_script.why: The child uses the property of the kite diagonals to draw a kite from its two diagonal lengths.
video_script.substitution: the book's question with diagonals of 6 cm and 8 cm
video_script.anchor: a kite drawn from the diagonal AC of 6 cm and the diagonal BD of 8 cm
video_script.payoff_line: The kite has diagonals of six and eight centimetres

final_answer.value: Kite ABCD with AC = 6 cm and BD = 8 cm; BD cuts AC in half at right angles, and O is not the middle of BD
final_answer.spoken: kite eigh B C D with eigh C of six centimetres and B D of eight centimetres, where B D cuts eigh C in half at right angles and O is not the middle of B D

hold_back: Kite ABCD with AC = 6 cm and BD = 8 cm; BD cuts AC in half at right angles, and O is not the middle of BD
never_show: the crossing O drawn at the middle of BD
maths_rules: AC = 6 cm is drawn first and its midpoint O is 3 cm from each end
the line at right angles through O carries the other diagonal
B is 2 cm from O on one side and D is 6 cm from O on the other side, so BD = 2 + 6 = 8 cm
B and D lie on the line at right angles through the middle of AC, so BA = BC and DA = DC
AB differs from AD, so ABCD is a kite and not a rhombus; O is not the middle of BD
video_script.design: One idea: the longer diagonal sits on the line through the middle of the shorter one. One drawing grows on the board in the order of the steps.
open_questions: The book gives only the two diagonal lengths; the 2 cm and 6 cm split of BD comes from the worklist.
